Retaining LiteTCN: model revisions and measured evidence

IE643 project technical notes · 19 October 2026 · Ayush Patel (23B0037), Rishik Yadav (23B2103).

Supporting experiment material, not the team's final assessment report. Original checkpoints and earlier experiments are preserved. Climate and energy received targeted new LiteTCN experiments; the existing finance results and models remain available.

Outcome

LiteTCN was retained and retrained. Both highlighted variants improve the original saved LiteTCN. Neither consistently beats the strongest existing hybrid/DLinear family. That is the measured reason for keeping alternatives available in the final system. The default LiteTCN selections demonstrate continuity with the project; they are not claimed to be the lowest-error methods.

Why the peaks and dips are difficult

The plots forecast the next 24 unseen hours, rather than reconstructing the observed input. Climate examples include both overprediction and underprediction: their actual/predicted maxima were 27.2/29.44, 31.5/29.50 and 16.1/17.31 degC. A blanket amplitude increase would worsen two examples. Daily amplitude changes, offsets and timing errors all matter.

Energy's prior source-training sample had a mean actual 24h range of 6.05 degC and a predicted range of 3.08 degC. Smoothing was therefore present before transfer. On 64 source examples, the earlier Patch MLP can reduce energy RMSE from 2.88 to 0.72 degC and restore most of the range. This shows capacity to fit that sample and functioning optimization; it does not establish an achievable test-error floor.

Pointwise MSE favors averages across uncertain futures. The available inputs contain past local weather/load measurements, but no future weather forecasts, regional spatial context or known future transformer dispatch. These missing drivers plausibly contribute to sudden changes; an irreducible-error bound has not been established. Small-batch fitting, validation overfitting and adaptation-proxy failures show that simply adding layers does not resolve the measured problem. All models forecast the horizon directly, so this is not recursive error accumulation.

LiteTCN v3: source-trained revision

A small dilated TCN is retained. Six daily cycles are folded into 24 hourly-position tokens; no hourly positions are averaged away. Four depthwise/pointwise residual blocks use dilations 1,2,4,8, with attention over observed tokens, a channel-specific linear skip, and optional known clock/week/year sine/cosine features. The effective history is 144 real hours, allowing a complete 144-to-24-hour pretext inside each 168-hour target input without padding. All 24 outputs are predicted directly. The model has 44,399 parameters.

Source controls: no-clock/MSE, clock/MSE, clock/shape.
Key variable weight: 3; other variables: 1.
Shape objective = weighted MSE + .25 ramp MSE + .1 max/min-value MSE.
Common selection score = .5 multivariate MSE + .5 key MSE
                       + .25 key peak/trough MSE + .1 key ramp MSE.

Each control uses the same 36 sampled rounds, up to 4,096 randomly drawn source windows per round, batch 256, AdamW 0.001, weight decay 0.0001 and cosine decay. These are sampled rounds, not 36 complete dataset passes. Source validation chooses the variant and checkpoint; clock/MSE wins on both datasets. The shape loss improves some extreme-value measurements but does not win the combined source criterion. Only the chosen variant is replicated across seeds 1 and 2; control ablations use seed 0.

Input-only adaptation = forecast loss on withheld values INSIDE each target X
                      + .25 source replay loss + .001 L2-SP.
10 sampled adaptation rounds, AdamW 0.0003, cosine decay.
Checkpoint proxy = .5 relative source-validation score
                 + .5 relative target-input-pretext score.
Reject source validation MSE increases above 10%; include the source fallback.

LiteTCN-R: preserve the original encoder

The original source-trained three-layer strided LiteTCN encoder and projection weights are retained exactly. DLinear's seasonal/trend operators are folded algebraically into the shared linear temporal skip; a zero neural head reproduces its source forecast. The residual head is fitted with source-only ridge regression and adapted using source replay, a source-head anchor and within-input forecast residuals. The encoder remains frozen. The unused reconstruction head is removed: 229,902 stored parameters, of which 21,672 belong to the updated head.

Residual adaptation = target-input forecast MSE + replay × source MSE
                    + anchor × ||head - source_head||².
Replay ∈ {.25, 1}; anchor ∈ {.001, .01, .1, 1, 10}.
Select per variable using source validation + target-input pretext,
with a 10% source guard and an explicit zero-residual baseline.

This controls how much a source-specific nonlinear residual can change the strong linear forecast. On energy the neural residual still slightly worsens overall target MSE compared with the linear skip alone. That negative result is retained; this model is not relabeled as a superior DLinear model.

Optional recent-residual correction

A separate LiteTCN v3 variant compares a forecast made 12 hours earlier with now-observed input values, then applies a bounded, decaying level/affine correction. Source validation and a nested target-input validation task select its strength. Windows reset independently, and no target forecasting labels are used. It gives modest near-term corrections rather than solving unseen peak changes.

New 2026 climate period

LiteTCN v3, its recent-residual policy, the original saved model and the previous hybrid were frozen and hashed before downloading Jan-Sep 2026 weather data. No subsequent model selection or training used that period for those frozen models. The LiteTCN-R extension is not claimed to have independent confirmation on this period. Each domain has 6,529 rolling 24-hour forecasts. Data and request metadata are cached separately under data/confirmatory_2026/climate.

CPU timings use one thread, five warmups and 30 repeats, with clock features prepacked. LiteTCN v3 stores fewer parameters but is slower per window than the original strided model. LiteTCN-R preserves its inference backbone and only updates a small head. Total original parameter counts include an unused reconstruction head; forecast-parameter counts exclude it.

Reproduction and verification

python -m src.peak_train --datasets climate energy --seeds 0 1 2 --epochs 36 --adapt-epochs 10 --max-windows 4096 --batch-size 256 --threads 4
python -m src.peak_calibrate --datasets climate energy --seeds 0 1 2
python -m src.residual_train --datasets climate energy --seeds 0 1 2
python -m src.peak_confirm
python -m src.check_peak
python -m src.peak_report
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
streamlit run app/app.py

The runners reuse the earlier saved source checkpoints in models/improved. Source/target chronological splits and scalers remain unchanged. Source labels are permitted; target weight fitting and selection use each individual input only, with no cross-window reconstruction of forecasting labels. The original development test has been observed repeatedly and is explicitly not an independent holdout. A final timing-log error in the first climate invocation was corrected after checkpoints and metrics had been saved; the original code snapshot/manifest and unchanged selection-freeze timestamp are retained.

All 24 regression tests passed, including 48 interface experiment/domain/dataset combinations, calendar alignment, encoder-gradient flow, within-input isolation, exact DLinear folding, residual-head scaling/order and checkpoint persistence. Source-only small-subset fitting checks were also run separately. The interface names every model family explicitly, supports source and target CSVs, and keeps stronger benchmark alternatives available.

Assessment use

The evidence supports an honest sequence: original LiteTCN, diagnosed smoothing/generalization, controlled architectural/loss experiments, retained-encoder residual adaptation, and comparison against stronger alternatives. Include negative results and explain why a deployment alternative is selected. No claim is made that a new architecture is a named-paper reproduction or that these changes guarantee a grade. The official template was verified against the supplied ZIP and saved unchanged under report/official_template; this supporting note is not a replacement for the team's own final report in that template.
